To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
testicular germ cell tumor (TGCT) is a disease with high aneuploidies and few somatic mutations.

1) TGCTs are highly aneuploid and have few somatic mutations, 2) KIT, KRas, and NRas mutations are associated with seminomas, 3) distinct molecular patterns are associated with the major histologic subtypes, 4) seminomas with mutations in KIT have increased immune infiltration and globally demethylated genomes, and 5) CpH methylation is associated with embryonal carcinomas.
we have performed a comprehensive molecular characterization of TGCTs and identified molecular subgroups of TGCTs that are associated with clinical features and histology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of germ cell tumors.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the pathophysiology of testicular germ cell tumours (TGCTs).
the identification of novel molecular targets and pathways for the development of new therapeutic approaches for TGCTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TGCTs are a genetically and epigenetically complex disease with a high degree of heterogeneity, and the molecular features of the disease may be used to improve risk stratification and to identify novel therapeutic targets.
the molecular landscape of TGCTs is complex and heterogeneous, with distinct patterns of genomic, epignomic, transcriptomic and proteomic changes that correlate with histology and clinical outcome.
